title: The Street of Crocodiles
significance: His debut story collection reorganizes his father's shop and the seasons of Drohobycz into mythic time; published on Zofia Nałkowska's recommendation, it introduced its then-unknown art-teacher author to the Polish literary world. It was printed in late 1933, though the title page carries the year 1934.

title: The Mythologizing of Reality
significance: A short manifesto arguing that words are originally fragments of myth and that poetry's task is to rejoin those fragments. It is the most compressed statement in which the author explains, in his own words, what his prose is trying to do.

title: Sanatorium Under the Sign of the Hourglass
significance: His second and final story collection, including the title story in which his dead father is alive again at a sanatorium where time has been turned back; it extends the world of the first collection into experiments with time.

title: The Comet
significance: A story in which a comet heading for Earth changes course and the apocalypse is called off; it is among the last stories he saw into print in his lifetime. It never made it into either story collection and appeared only in a magazine.

title: Ferdydurke
significance: In a premise where a thirty-year-old writer is dragged off by a teacher and turned back into a schoolboy, the novel demonstrates through comic plot how the social Form of maturity is imposed on people. His key vocabulary of 'immaturity' and the 'mug' was established here.

title: Ivona, Princess of Burgundia
significance: A play in which simply bringing an almost silent woman into the court is enough to make the entire court trip over its own Form and collapse. This structure, which makes silence the engine of the stage, is often compared to postwar Theatre of the Absurd.

title: Trans-Atlantyk
significance: Narrated by a Pole stranded in Buenos Aires in 1939, it recounts duty to the homeland and liberation from that duty in a style parodying the old Polish oral-narrative form (gawęda). The book collided head-on with the émigré Polish community.

title: Diary
significance: Serialized in the Paris émigré journal Kultura and later collected into three volumes, this is not a private record but takes the form of a public argument against Polishness, Catholicism, and literary authority. The serialization began in 1953 and continued almost until his death.

title: Pornografia
significance: Set in the Polish countryside under German occupation, the novel follows two middle-aged men who stage-manage a young man and woman toward each other. The very gaze that spies on and manipulates youth becomes the engine of the narrative.

title: Cosmos
significance: A novel in which the narrator obsessively builds chains of meaning out of trivial signs — a hanged sparrow, a stain on the ceiling — turning the detective-novel form into an experiment in the compulsion to interpret. It won the Prix International in 1967.

title: The Sleepwalkers
significance: A trilogy that renders 1888, 1903, and 1918 in the styles of Romanticism, anarchy, and matter-of-factness respectively, with the final volume inserting an essay chapter titled 'The Disintegration of Values' between the narrative sections. The first two volumes appeared in 1931 and the last in 1932.

title: James Joyce and the Present Age
significance: A lecture text that reads Ulysses as a form of cognition attempting to hold the totality of its age, it also serves as Broch's own theoretical account of what his own novels are trying to do.

title: The Death of Virgil
significance: A novel narrating the last eighteen hours of Virgil, who wants to burn the Aeneid, divided into four parts named water, fire, earth, and air; it asks whether art is justified in the face of death and politics. Completed in exile in the United States, the German and English editions appeared together in 1945.

title: The Guiltless
significance: Eleven stories set against the backdrop of 1913, 1923, and 1933 are woven into a single novel, showing how the 'guiltlessness' of people who did not actively participate in Nazism becomes another name for political indifference.

title: The Wedding
significance: A play in which characters gathered in a tenement building on the verge of collapse each rant about possessiveness before the building comes down. His method of constructing each character solely through a fixed manner of speech, an 'acoustic mask,' was first carried out here.

title: Auto-da-Fé
significance: A novel in which a sinologist living among twenty-five thousand books collides with the world through marriage to his housekeeper and finally burns along with his library. Written in 1930–31 and published in 1935, it is the only novel he left.

title: Crowds and Power
significance: A study built from cases in myth, ritual, and political history that theorizes how crowds arise and what types they take, and that defines the man of power as 'the survivor.' It is his central work, written over some thirty years following the experience of the crowd he underwent at the 1927 burning of the Vienna Palace of Justice.

title: The Voices of Marrakesh
significance: A record of his 1954 stay in Marrakesh that chooses to observe a language he cannot understand purely as sound, turning the travelogue into a record of hearing.

title: The Tongue Set Free
significance: The first volume of his three-part autobiography, covering his Ladino-speaking childhood in Ruse through the German his mother forced him to acquire, explaining through scenes of language acquisition why he came to write in German.

title: The Black Heralds
significance: His first poetry collection inherits the musicality of Modernismo while drawing the Catholicism, family, and guilt of the rural Andes into poetic material. The title page carries the year 1918, but actual distribution took place in 1919.

title: Trilce
significance: Across 77 poems, spelling and syntax are deliberately destroyed and numbers, blank spaces, and coinages are introduced, reenacting the experience of imprisonment and loss at the level of notation itself. The first edition was printed at a press inside a Lima prison.

title: Tungsten
significance: A novel dealing with foreign capital and indigenous labor at an Andean mine, it is an exceptional work in which he set aside his poetic experiments and adopted the grammar of the proletarian novel.

title: Human Poems
significance: A collection of poems accumulated during his Paris exile, gathered by his widow Georgette Vallejo after his death and published in Paris in 1939. It reattaches the experiment of Trilce to human time through a vocabulary of hunger, illness, and the laboring body.

title: Spain, Take This Cup from Me
significance: Fifteen poems written during the Spanish Civil War that mourn Republican soldiers and the people while holding to a language of the body and of prayer rather than slogans. It appeared as a book in 1939, the year after his death.

title: Evening
significance: Her first collected volume of short lyric poems that fix an emotional moment through a single concrete object or gesture, it became a working example of Acmeist poetics.

title: Rosary
significance: Her second collection, reprinted repeatedly in pre-revolutionary Petersburg, made her a leading poet of her time. Within the form of the short love poem, it pushed narrative omission to its limit.

title: White Flock
significance: A collection published on the threshold of war and revolution, it marks the beginning of a shift in which the vocabulary of love poetry starts to admit historical time.

title: Requiem
significance: A cycle written between 1935 and 1940, it takes as its speaker's position the line of women standing outside a Leningrad prison after her son's arrest. Publication was impossible inside the Soviet Union, and the text survived only through recitation and memorization until a first Russian edition appeared in Munich in 1963 without the author's involvement; publication inside the Soviet Union came only in 1987.

title: The Flight of Time
significance: The last selected-poems volume to appear in the Soviet Union in her lifetime, arranged by the author herself with poems ranging from her early work to her final years. Censorship kept Requiem out of it.

title: Evening Album
significance: Her first collection, self-published at eighteen, brought her immediately into the literary world with reviews from Bryusov, Gumilyov, and Voloshin. Though it takes childhood and the family as its material, her characteristic directness of speech is already present.

title: Craft
significance: A collection published in Berlin, under a title that defines poetry not as inspiration but as labor done by hand, in which the syntax of compression and rupture begins in earnest.

title: Poem of the End
significance: A long poem written out of a few hours spent walking Prague while parting from a man, it advances the time of the separation using nothing but fragments of dialogue and dashes. Written in 1924 and published in 1926.

title: After Russia
significance: Her last collection published in her lifetime, issued in Paris and gathering poems from the early years of her exile. She published no new collection for the rest of her life.

title: My Pushkin
significance: Prose written for the centenary of Pushkin's death, it restores, in place of the public portrait of the national poet, the Pushkin a child met through a painting in the house and a forbidden book.

title: Buried Alive
significance: His first story collection, with a title story consisting of the monologue of a narrator about to take his own life, brought first-person psychological narration into Persian prose.

title: Three Drops of Blood
significance: A story collection whose title story features a narrator confined in a psychiatric hospital who undermines the reliability of his own narration; it gathers many of his best-known stories.

title: The Blind Owl
significance: A novella whose narrator, who does nothing but draw the same picture over and over on a pen-case lid, lives through the same event again across two different eras, dismantling both causality and the sense of time in Persian prose together. Publication was impossible inside Iran, so it first appeared in Bombay in a mimeographed edition of fifty copies, and it was first made public in Tehran through newspaper serialization in 1941.

title: The Stray Dog
significance: A story collection whose title story sustains, to the end, the point of view of a dog wandering a marketplace after losing its owner; it is the most widely read of his later stories.

title: Haji Aqa
significance: A satirical novella centered on the merchant Haji Aqa, who shifts his position with the direction of power; it takes direct aim at the political opportunism of an Iran that had gone through war and occupation.
